sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Oval-leaf huckleberry is a deciduous shrub with erect or spreading branches, about 0.4–4 m tall. It is native along the North Pacific coast, where plants may become low and bushy in exposed or heavily browsed sites.

sections.title: Flowers and berries
sections.text: Its oval leaves accompany pink, bell-shaped flowers and dark blue, wax-coated berries. The berries are gathered as food in Alaska and were an important traditional food for Indigenous peoples of Alaska and British Columbia. The plate’s leaves, pink bells and blue fruit fit this species.
